title: The Woodpecker and the Lion
author: Ellen C. Babbitt
summary: 啄木鸟救了狮子，狮子却不肯说一句谢谢。
publicDomainBasis: Retold by Ellen C. Babbitt and published in 1922 by The Century Co. (pre-1923, public domain in the United States); Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: One day while a Lion was eating his dinner a bone stuck in his throat. It hurt so that he could not finish his dinner. He walked up and down, up and down, roaring with pain.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，一头狮子正在吃晚饭，一根骨头卡在了喉咙里。疼得它吃不下饭，走来走去，痛得直吼。

paragraphs.en: A Woodpecker lit on a branch of a tree near-by, and hearing the Lion, she said, "Friend, what ails you?" The Lion told the Woodpecker what the matter was, and the Woodpecker said: "I would take the bone out of your throat, friend, but I do not dare to put my head into your mouth, for fear I might never get it out again. I am afraid you might eat me."
paragraphs.zh: 一只啄木鸟落在附近一棵树的枝头，听见狮子的吼声，便问：“朋友，你怎么了？”狮子把缘由告诉啄木鸟，啄木鸟说：“朋友，我倒是可以把骨头从你喉咙里取出来，可我不敢把头伸进你嘴里，怕再也出不来。我怕你把我吃了。”

paragraphs.en: "O Woodpecker, do not be afraid," the Lion said. "I will not eat you. Save my life if you can!"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，啄木鸟，别怕，”狮子说，“我不会吃你。你救救我的命吧！”

paragraphs.en: "I will see what I can do for you," said the Woodpecker. "Open your mouth wide." The Lion did as he was told, but the Woodpecker said to himself: "Who knows what this Lion will do? I think I will be careful."
paragraphs.zh: “我看看能为你做什么，”啄木鸟说，“把嘴张大。”狮子照办了，可啄木鸟心里想：“谁知道这狮子会干出什么来？我看还是小心点。”

paragraphs.en: So the Woodpecker put a stick between the Lion's upper and lower jaws so that he could not shut his mouth.
paragraphs.zh: 于是啄木鸟把一根小棍支在狮子上下牙之间，让它合不拢嘴。

paragraphs.en: Then the Woodpecker hopped into the Lion's mouth and hit the end of the bone with his beak. The second time he hit it, the bone fell out.
paragraphs.zh: 然后啄木鸟跳进狮子嘴里，用喙去敲骨头的末端。敲第二下时，骨头掉了出来。

paragraphs.en: The Woodpecker hopped out of the Lion's mouth, and hit the stick so that it too fell out. Then the Lion could shut his mouth.
paragraphs.zh: 啄木鸟跳出狮子的嘴，又去敲那根小棍，小棍也掉了下来。狮子这才合上了嘴。

paragraphs.en: At once the Lion felt very much better, but not one word of thanks did he say to the Woodpecker.
paragraphs.zh: 狮子顿时舒服多了，却一个字也没向啄木鸟道谢。

paragraphs.en: One day later in the summer, the Woodpecker said to the Lion, "I want you to do something for me."
paragraphs.zh: 夏天里有一天，啄木鸟对狮子说：“我想请你帮我做件事。”

paragraphs.en: "Do something for you?" said the Lion. "You mean you want me to do something more for you. I have already done a great deal for you. You cannot expect me to do anything more for you. Do not forget that once I had you in my mouth, and I let you go. That is all that you can ever expect me to do for you."
paragraphs.zh: “帮你做事？”狮子说，“你是说还想让我为你多做点事。我已经为你做了很多了。你别指望我再为你做什么。别忘了，我曾经把你含在嘴里，又放了你。我能为你做的，最多就是这样了。”

paragraphs.en: The Woodpecker said no more, but he kept away from the Lion from that day on.
paragraphs.zh: 啄木鸟没再说什么，可从那天起，它就远远躲着狮子。
